name: Haldor the Anvil-Father
portfolio: craft, oaths, the hearth of the hold
symbol: an anvil ringed by a band of gold
text: Haldor struck the first mountain on his anvil and taught the dwarves that a thing made well is a prayer that outlasts the maker. His priests keep the oath-rolls of their clans and bless every new forge with a coal carried from the old one.

name: Aurel of the Open Hand
portfolio: trade, honest weight, the road between markets
symbol: an open hand holding a balanced coin
text: Aurel walks the caravan roads as a pedlar who never cheats and is never cheated. Merchants tithe a coin from their first sale of the day, and a bargain sealed in her name is held binding in any market from the coast to the hills.

name: Ostrava of the Even Scale
portfolio: law, justice, oaths sworn before witnesses
symbol: a blindfold draped over a balanced scale
text: Ostrava gave up her eyes so that she would judge without favour. Her paladins ride circuit to towns too small for a magistrate, and her temples keep the town's laws written on the inside of their doors.

name: The Pale Ferryman
portfolio: death, rightful passage, the end of every road
symbol: a lantern hung from a ferry pole
text: The Ferryman takes every soul across the last river and turns none away, but he hates those who cheat the crossing. His priests sit with the dying, bury the dead with a coin for the fare, and hunt the walking dead without mercy.

name: Sylvaine of the Green Hush
symbol: an oak leaf with a drop of dew
text: Sylvaine is the silence that falls in a forest when something old is watching. The elves call her mother, farmers leave the last sheaf in the field for her, and woodcutters ask her pardon before the first cut of the day.

name: The Hollow King
portfolio: undeath, the hunger that outlasts the grave, secrets of the tomb
symbol: an empty crown on a skull with no jaw
text: The Hollow King promises the desperate that death need not be the end, and keeps the promise in the worst way. He has no temples, only cellars, and his choirs sing in the dark to wake what the Ferryman has already carried away.

name: Thrask the Iron Crown
portfolio: tyranny, conquest, the chain and the whip
symbol: a black gauntlet closed around a crown
text: Thrask teaches that the strong owe the weak nothing but orders. Warlords pray to him before a siege, and petty tyrants keep his symbol under their robes of office.

name: The Lantern Mother
portfolio: dawn, healing, hope, the lamp left burning for travellers
symbol: a hand cupped around a lantern flame
text: Every frontier town keeps a lamp in a window for the Lantern Mother, so that no traveller is lost in the dark. Her clerics heal without asking who is paying, and her shrines are the first holy places raised in a new settlement.

name: Ghorvak the One-Eyed
portfolio: slaughter, the horde, the eye that never closes
symbol: a single bloodshot eye on a spearhead
text: Ghorvak put out his own eye to see only war. The orc warbands carry his spear at their head, and their shamans read his will in the smoke of burning villages.

name: Brannoch of the Red Banner
portfolio: courage, honourable battle, soldiers and sellswords
symbol: a red banner on a broken spear
text: Brannoch does not care which side wins, only that it is fought bravely. Soldiers swear by his banner, sellswords pay his priests to bless their blades, and cowards are said to hear his laughter in their sleep.

name: The Stormmother
portfolio: storms, the sea, the luck of those who sail
symbol: a trident wrapped in a lightning bolt
text: The Stormmother is fickle and proud. Sailors throw her a coin before every voyage, and towns that forget her offerings learn what her rain can do to a harvest.

name: Nim of the Veiled Coin
portfolio: thieves, luck, secrets, the card turned at the last moment
symbol: a coin half hidden behind a grey veil
text: Nim is the god of everything that changes hands without anyone noticing. Gamblers kiss a coin for luck, thieves leave a stolen trinket at his hidden altars, and every guild of the night claims him as its founder.

name: Ysolde of the Unshut Book
portfolio: lore, invention, maps, the wish to know
symbol: an open book with an eye on each page
text: Ysolde keeps a book that never closes, and every true thing ever learned is written in it. Wizards dedicate their spellbooks to her, cartographers ink her eye in the corner of their maps, and her priests trade secrets the way merchants trade salt.
